title: Prosperity - Not Austerity
summary:
Prosperity - Not Austerity
After making a quiet entrance into President Obama's cabinet, Steven Chu, the new US Energy Secretary has found himself in the limelight. Perhaps less by choice and more because of a call by media and lawmakers, Chu has gone from a Nobel Prize winning physicist, to a man with the power to shape and mold the future of US energy policy and arguably the world. While it is yet to be determined if Chu's basket of ideas parallel President Obama's, his comments of late have provided insight into his disconnection from oil.

children.summary: US GDP Using change in GDP as a metric of the US economy, the correlation to WTI is insignificant. Instead of hanging the health of the economy on the price of crude oil (either positive or negative), perhaps more attention should be paid to the detrimental affects of policy.

children.title: Flower Power
children.summary: After oil peaked in July 2008 + $147/bbl, the sleeping green giant was awakened by new advocates for fuel efficient cars, hydrogen power, fuel cells and any other means of transport which could stave off prices at the pump. As the dust settled, policy makers found themselves in a new battleground; energy was called to the plate.

children.title: Green Job Training
children.summary:
Only in the past month have rough plans been hewn out for the public - which includes $60 billion in the near term and $150 billion over the next ten years to be invested into green technology. However, a quick scan of the energy portion of the American Recovery Act leaves members of the petroleum industry empty handed as funds have been diverted for the strict use of creating green jobs and retooling the US to become a renewable powerhouse and "exporter of renewable energy."
"So we have a choice to make.

children.title: The Green Curtain
children.summary: While Washington has yet to determine the ultimate direction of their actions, the scheduled timeline for serious policy decisions seems short. On one hand, President Obama has declared energy independence from foreign oil and unveiled a massive green spending package.
